name: Fairmont Golden Prague
positioning: Fairmont hotel in a 1974 brutalist building in Prague, with six restaurants and bars and a spa
best_for: Travelers who like design and architecture
Food lovers who want several dining venues under one roof

facts.text: Fairmont Golden Prague blends brutalist grandeur with Czech artistry and modern elegance.
The hotel is set in a brutalist building from 1974.
The building was designed by Czech architect Karel Filsak and originally opened as the InterContinental Prague.
The hotel has six restaurants and bars serving Czech, Asian and European flavors, including Zlatá Praha, Greenhouse and the rooftop bar Golden Eye.
The fine-dining restaurant Zlata Praha is on the top floor and has views over the spires and towers of the Old Town.
The first-floor Greenhouse serves an all-day menu of beer-hall favorites.
The spa has three saunas, a steam room, and treatment rooms for massages and facials.
The spa offers a signature Czech Crystal Beauty facial, a 90-minute treatment that uses crystals.
The Old Town Square is a short walk from the hotel.
The Vltava River can be walked along or crossed to reach Prague Castle.
Rooms have a 55 inch TV, Nespresso machine, Dyson Supersonic hair dryer and Le Labo bathroom amenities.
Fairmont Gold rooms are on the high floors, with private check-in, concierge service and access to an exclusive lounge.

considerations.text: Parking is available for an additional fee.
Pets are welcome but not permitted within the restaurant, spa and bar premises.
